lines.t: The pillars hummed a full octave when you won. They haven't done that since Dorran's own trial. He pretends not to remember.
Both rows have sunk. The way to the dais is clear. Cantor Dorran is waiting — and he's a patient waiter.
Welcome to Knell Hall. The pillars here are tuned stone. Out-sing a hall Tuner and their row sinks into the floor.
Two Tuners, two rows. Then Cantor Dorran Shale. His kin are stone, like the hall — verdant and water voices do well here.
And do mind the tuning plates. They're for looking at. Last week someone licked one.
You came up the ridge road. I heard you from the heather. So did the stone.
Stone keeps time better than any clock. Let's see if you do.
Steady hands. Steady head. You'd have made a fair quarryman.
Keynote's yours. Tuned to toxin. Odd pairing, stone and rot — but rot's how stone becomes soil.
And an Etude — Rock Tumble. Teach it to a kin that doesn't mind getting dusty.
The coil crews went down the Undertone yesterday. Miners are not pleased. Neither's the mountain.
Kett says you opened a Stillmark pen and walked his crew's kin home. Good. The mountain's humming easier.
Sallowfen's past the up-shaft. Soft ground. Step like you're sorry.

I've had the quarry lift unchained for you. West end of town. Take your stone kin — the lower galleries want shifting.

Steady hands. Steady head. You'd have made a fair quarryman.
Rushed it. Stone doesn't rush. Try again when you've counted to ten.
